tob-10813: Written just before his conversion to Catholicism, Newman’s famous essay argues that Christian doctrine was not fixed once and for all but grew and deepened across the centuries — like a seed becoming a tree. tob-0213: G. K. Chesterton’s nightmare-farce trails the poet-detective Syme into a ring of anarchists — each named for a weekday — in a chase that turns the world head over heels. tob-9047-61113: The fourth volume of Pliny’s Natural History treats cures drawn from beasts — and the wonder-working, old wives’ lore, and quackery tangled with them. It is the old world’s medicine chest, gripping and gruesome by turns. Bostock’s English keeps every strange receipt.
tob-4113: Max Müller’s first Upanishad volume opened the Sacred Books of the East series itself — the Chandogya and fellow early Upanishads in English dress. tob-12913: Annie Besant’s Ancient Wisdom — 1897 — is the classic popular Theosophy text, summarizing the Secret Doctrine’s vast cosmic system. Her clear exposition made Theosophy accessible to thousands of readers. The book remains the best general introduction to the movement.
tob-0039-d13: This microfilm roll carries a piece of the Doctors’ Trial record at Nuremberg — the official account of the Nazi doctors’ trial. Proof, exhibits, and rulings stand here in full. Every page serves the historical record. Scholars prize the whole set for its fullness.
arxiv-2605-08913: Running a language model on a Mac should get faster as you shrink the workload — but sometimes it does not. arxiv-2605-09113: Real storage media forbid certain patterns — and still demand error correction. arxiv-2605-09313: Diffusion transformers develop attention sinks — tokens that hog attention for no clear reason, warping the generation. arxiv-2605-09413: Saying the right words in the wrong tone ruins the message — expressive appropriateness matters. Tianrui Wang, Ziyang Ma, Yizhou Peng, and colleagues evaluate it for speech in rich contexts. The 2026 paper judges not what voices say, but how fittingly they say it.
arxiv-2605-09513: Long-horizon trackers drift — slowly losing their target — and need semantic watchdogs. arxiv-2605-09713: Rare-earth nickelates hide a non-magnetic insulating phase born from the Jahn-Teller effect — lattice distortions that split electron orbitals. Sangeeta Rajpurohit, Liang Z. arxiv-2605-10013: LLMs infer personas from user data — but when is that inference acceptable? arxiv-2605-10113: Motzkin paths with two variants of level steps on odd levels, counted via the classical kernel method. Helmut Prodinger develops the enumeration carefully. arxiv-2605-10413: Jet evolution in the glasma — the pre-equilibrium quark-gluon state — via light-front Hamiltonians. Dana Avramescu, Carlos Lamas, Tuomas Lappi, and colleagues track the evolution. The 2026 paper is QCD. It evolves jets through the glasma via light-front Hamiltonians.
arxiv-2605-10613: Neural ODEs with exact fixed-point constraints and provable universality. Feliciano Giuseppe Pacifico develops the architecture. The 2026 paper is deep learning theory. plos-pone-0003813: Edwards, Fridley, and James tightened the rules for gene-hunt replication in this 2008 paper. Their evaluation of clustering and genotype distribution gives genome-wide association studies a better way to confirm hits. The methods raise the bar for claiming a gene-disease link.

plos-pone-0354813: ‘It would be really great if I had greater confidence and ability there’ — primary care doctors’ candid words on nutrition. plos-pone-0354713: Medium-voltage switchgears — the grid’s workhorses — need health assessment and failure prediction. This paper built an integrated Gaussian–probabilistic–fuzzy framework for both. plos-pone-0352813: CAR-T cell therapy — 7x19 dosing — recipient immune cell gene expression profiled in syngeneic mice. This paper did so. The profiling revealed how the engineered cells reshape host immunity. The findings guided the dosing of living drugs — cellular therapy’s pharmacology.

plos-pone-0354013: Pisolithus arhizus metabolites — targeting mastitis Staphylococcus aureus efflux pumps — computationally and experimentally evaluated. This paper did so. plos-pone-0351113: AI rate integrator — calibration and sensitivity enhancement through EKF, with impact on Raman spectroscopy wavelengths. This paper did so. The analysis tuned the sensor and the spectrum together. The finding sharpens both. The work calibrates the instrument and its light.
plos-pone-0351313: Six tumor invasion and metastasis markers including MMP-9 — simultaneously detected by a microfluidic chip-based magnetic particle immunoassay. This methodological study built it. europmc-pmc2807913: Plants sense drought through the hormone abscisic acid, and this 2010 paper fills in a missing link in that chain. europmc-pmc2826413: The Parkinson's-tied protein DJ-1 guards the cell's power packs. This 2010 paper shows that losing DJ-1 cuts the cell's self-cleaning and wrecks power-pack upkeep. The team traces how its loss lets harm pile up. The work ties one gene to the cell faults behind Parkinson's.
europmc-pmc2831913: Air pollution does not hit men and women identically. This 2010 paper argues for a growing role of gender analysis in air pollution epidemiology. europmc-pmc2852313: Coot lets researchers build and fix protein models by hand on screen, turning raw X-ray data into finished structures. europmc-pmc2855713: Green tea compounds are tested against cancer cells with color-change assays, but this 2010 paper warns the tests can lie. europmc-pmc3017113: Insect-killing fungi got their genomes read. This 2011 paper sequences two Metarhizium fungi and compares their active genes. The authors reveal the killers' toolkit. europmc-pmc3228813: The genome's repeats got bigger. This 2011 paper argues repeats may fill over two-thirds of the human genome. The authors revise the count upward. Their work reshaped genomics. Old estimates said half, they show. The repeats shape evolution, they argue.

europmc-pmc3356313: COPD got an inflammation warning. This 2012 paper links lasting inflammation to poor COPD outcomes. The authors reveal the pattern. Their work guides treatment. Agustí's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It shaped COPD care. The study is a classic.

gao-gaoreports-b-297413: Puglia Engineering tripled its January 2006 protest — three case numbers, one shipyard fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles all. The firm challenged the awards, and the call weighs each claim. Triple filings get one careful answer. Three dockets, one fair verdict.
gao-gaoreports-b-297313: PHT Corporation took its December 2005 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Every challenger gets the full fair-play hearing.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-13: The Pentagon's resource decisions needed better risk analysis in 2005, and GAO's report says additional actions were needed to enhance the approach. The findings demand the rigor. The report warns that the defense dollars deserved careful choices. The actions had to be taken.
gao-gaoreports-gao-05-813: Workplace immigration raids were falling flat in 2005, and GAO's report says the weak tools failed the job. The findings demand the fixes. The report warns that the illegal hiring deserved stopping. The illegal hiring deserved stopping. The tools had to be fixed.
openalex-w7207867013: Can practicing on actors make medical students more caring doctors? Researchers at a medical school in western Parana, Brazil, measured students' empathy before and after simulated patient consultations, practice visits with trained stand-ins. Using a before-and-after design, the study tests whether rehearsal builds the human side of medicine. The result speaks to a simple idea: empathy can be taught, and practice is how.
openalex-w7205009213: What happens to mining engineers after graduation? This study tracks 548 graduates of the Federal University of Ouro Preto from 2013 to 2023, drawing on surveys of 125 alumni plus faculty records. The picture is tough: new graduates face outsized demands for prior experience, software skills, and English, and nearly half of jobs come through personal contacts. A data-rich reality check on the path from engineering degree to mining job.
openalex-w7205013813: Septic shock is the deadliest face of sepsis, and survival depends on speed. This literature review surveys current strategies for the early management of septic shock: recognizing it fast and acting immediately. The authors synthesize what intensive care research says about the measures that save lives in the first critical hours. A clinical review where the takeaway is blunt, in septic shock, delay kills.
arxiv-2606-16013: Multiple linear regression is one of the simplest statistical tools, and people trust it because it seems interpretable. This paper asks how far that trust should go: where exactly does interpretability break down, even in this easy case? The authors map the limits, giving data scientists a clearer sense of when "I can explain this model" stops being true.
arxiv-2606-16113: When an AI denies someone a loan or a job, the person deserves to know what would change the outcome — that's "algorithmic recourse." RecourseBench is a modular framework for testing recourse methods reproducibly, so researchers can compare them fairly. The paper presents the benchmark for the fairness-and-explainability research community.
arxiv-2606-16313: Self-driving cars predict where nearby vehicles will go, and rare, unusual trajectories (the "long tail") are where predictions fail dangerously. This paper asks whether trajectory displacement — how far a predicted path strays — is a safe measure in those rare cases. It targets autonomous-driving researchers worried about the edge cases that matter most.
arxiv-2606-16413: Imagine controlling a robot arm with your thoughts while seeing through its eyes in augmented reality. This paper builds a brain-robot interface with AR feedback for generalist robot-arm manipulation — one system handling many tasks. It targets researchers in brain-computer interfaces and assistive robotics.
arxiv-2606-16613: What brews when bot hordes swap, spar, and team up for the long haul? CoffeeBench drops long-game bot minds into mixed trade worlds — odd bots, odd jobs — and scores the brew. For herd-mind fans who watch bot bazaars bloom.
